svg.title: Walking a fallback chain with a recorded reason beside every model
svg.desc: A request walks an ordered chain. The first model sat out a rate-limit cooldown, the second was paused by the operator, the third answered, and the rest were never reached. The request log lists every entry with its reason, so a fallback is never invisible.

g.text: The router stops at the first attempt that succeeds. A skipped entry costs no attempt and no deadline.
A run of failures on one model moves to the next model; only auth, 429 and transport faults try another key.
A 429 benches the (key, model) pair, not the whole key, and the key keeps serving its other models.
Why a body that fails is not retried forever
Timeouts, 5xx, a 410 and a plain 400 are properties of the model or the moment, and
every key in the pool would meet the same answer.
Those raise out of the rotating loop so the chain spends its time on a different model
instead of the rest of the pool.
Failover happens before the first streamed chunk; after output starts, a failure is
